definition.name: Doorbell chime
definition.description: A low-voltage sounder controlled by a separate pushbutton.

terminals.label: L
terminals.purpose: First low-voltage sounder connection, across the isolated transformer secondary through the doorbell push. L/N are retained model identifiers; this lesson supplies AC at the declared secondary voltage, not 240 V mains.

terminals.label: N
terminals.purpose: Second low-voltage sounder connection, across the isolated transformer secondary through the doorbell push. L/N are retained model identifiers; this lesson supplies AC at the declared secondary voltage, not 240 V mains.

parts.name: Housing
parts.purpose: The enclosure supports and separates functional parts. This original teaching model is representative equipment, not a manufacturer drawing.

parts.name: Removable cover
parts.purpose: The cover limits access to internal connections. Opening it here is a virtual inspection operation.

parts.name: Terminal clamps
parts.purpose: Metal clamps establish connections to individual conductors. The circuit engine connects terminal IDs, not the apparent proximity of 3D wires.

parts.name: Mounting and fixings
parts.purpose: Mounting hardware supports the equipment. Screws, rail clips and glands are modelled separately from electrical connections.

parts.name: Electromagnetic coil
parts.purpose: Voltage across the coil produces a magnetic operating force. This simulation models coil demand and pickup, rather than magnetic field saturation or inrush.

parts.name: Operating mechanism
parts.purpose: The mechanism translates a handle, button, coil or control demand into an operating state.
